It feeds the day-length beat (docs/design/earth-level-brief.md, beat 10),
which closes the causal chain rotation -> tilt -> day length. The bars are
CONTINUOUS UNLABELLED ARCS: no ticks, no segments, no hour count, no times.
A segmented clock face is an hour count in disguise and rule 2 bars it.
The four instants are also in data/generated/orbital-positions.json under
`seasons`; the two must name the same days, which a test asserts.
The equinox day is SEVEN MINUTES LONGER than twelve hours, because of
atmospheric refraction and because sunrise is measured from the first edge
of the Sun's disc rather than its centre. Do not draw the equinox arcs as

location.note: The city name here is metadata, not player text. Every player-facing string lives in content/bg/ (rule 3).

sourceName: U.S. Naval Observatory, Astronomical Applications Department, sun rise/set service

note: Bulgarian civil time: EET (UTC+02) in winter, EEST (UTC+03) in summer.
The offset on each row is the one in force on that date, and it is
confirmed by the data itself -- the midpoint of each sunrise/sunset pair
lands on local solar noon for Sofia's longitude only under the offset
docs/sources.md records only these four days for Sofia. A month-by-month
curve would have to be retrieved from the same USNO service and recorded
there first; typing one from memory is exactly what rule 1 forbids. The
beat compares the four season days, which is what it needs.
